I've gotten a recurring question in the last 24 hours.

"Sully, how did you so accurately predict that Bitcoin was about to explode?"

1) I've seen the future.

2) It is orange.

In all seriousness, though, a lot of luck was involved in the timing. But people assumed a massive, fearful event was coming. They thought it would be obvious and that they'd get the juicy entry they'd been planning.

That's not how bears work.

People stop giving a damn.

So this is what I've been hyper-focused on. Watching for signs of boredom. I did a bunch of analysis on short-term traders, but my favorite signal was this chart.

It looks wild if it’s the first time you’ve seen it, but bear with me because it’s very high-signal IMO.

It lets us visualize how frequently people have mentioned Bitcoin price targets using a heatmap.

The higher the density, the “hotter” the color (note the bright red when we first broke through $100k in 2024).

You can literally see the boredom here.

People stopped making price predictions in either direction.

Bitcoin stopped being interesting.

This doesn't tell the whole story. It can't tell us when liquidity will be injected into the system or when a new buyer is entering the market. 

But it can help us see when all the hot money has moved onto other things.

Historically, this is quite bullish.

It certainly was this time 🍻

So, hold on, let me get this straight. So the tradfi guys who were bloviating incessantly about Bitcoin being little more than levered QQQ were completely wrong this entire time? Consider me shocked. I used to think some of these guys had an IQ above 80.

BREAKING: The Cass Freight Index fell -4.8% YoY in July, to 0.96, matching the lowest level since the 2020 pandemic.

The index tracks freight shipment activity across North America and is a widely followed indicator of freight demand.

This marks the 42nd consecutive monthly decline, the longest streak on record.

Over this period, shipments have fallen -20%, with the index declining -7.0% in 2023, -5.8% in 2024, and -7.5% in 2025.

MoM, shipments posted their 3rd consecutive monthly decline, reversing the brief rebound seen earlier this year.

This decline reflects higher fuel prices, while a renewed driver shortage is reducing available trucking capacity and weighing on shipment volumes.

The US freight market continues to weaken.

With the caveat that I am anything but an expert on AI, based on some great conversations with our internal thought leaders in recent weeks it seems that there are two risks to the AI boom. One risk is the potential commodification of the US frontier models, which are big spenders in the AI space but which might have problems raising capital if their closed models get disrupted by the cheaper open-weight models. It appears this may be happening as the Silicon Data Token Expenditure index might suggest.

What could that mean for the hyperscalers and their capex? Most of this cohort consists of big companies with thriving business, which could survive a downtick in capex (if not benefit from it).

The other risk may be all the capital raising that is happening in the bond market. The Semiconductor Lease Rates chart shows half a trillion of issuance this year and possibly more next year. What could happen to the value of this debt when the semiconductor leases are up for renewal against an uncertain depreciation and supply backdrop? For now, chip rental prices are holding steady and demand seems to be way ahead of supply, so perhaps this is a risk down the road.

BREAKING: The average price of US ground beef jumped +9% YoY in July, to a record $7.10 per pound.

Ground beef prices have surged +65% since the end of 2019. 

Meanwhile, steak prices surged +10% YoY last month, to a record $13.10 per pound, up +70% since December 2019.

As a result, beef sales volumes fell -0.3% YoY over the 13 weeks ending mid-July..

This is a sharp reversal from +5.4% YoY growth during the same period in 2025, and +4.6% YoY growth in 2024.

Americans are reducing beef consumption amid rapidly surging prices.
